sentences.text: The generic name Abditosaurus translates to "forgotten reptile," a title reflecting the long period during which the fossil remains remained hidden before being fully collected.
The type specimen is the most complete titanosaur skeleton known in Europe, notably preserving twelve of the estimated fourteen cervical vertebrae.
Complete or nearly complete neck sequences are very rare in sauropods; by early 2022, only 27 sauropod specimens with complete or nearly complete necks had been reported.
It was the first semi-articulated titanosaur specimen discovered in Europe.
German paleontologist Walter Georg Kühne uncovered the remains of a massive titanosaur on September 25, 1954, at the Orcau-1 site in Conques, Catalonia, Spain.
This find marked the first major sauropod discovery in Spain.
In 1956, Albert-Félix de Lapparent and Emiliano Aguirre assigned the fossil material to an unnamed species of the dubious genus Hypselosaurus.
Additional expeditions to the area were led by Josep Vicenç Santafé in 1984 and 1986, assisted by researchers from the Institute of Ilerda Studies in Lleida.
An expedition took place between 2012 and 2014 involving the Catalan Institute of Paleontology, the University of Zaragoza, and the Museum of Isona and Conca Dellà.
Parts of the initial findings were formally described in 2017.

The type species Abditosaurus kuehnei was named and described in 2022 by Bernat Vila, Albert Sellés, Miguel Moreno-Azanza, Novella L. Razzolini, Alejandro Gil-Delgado, José Ignacio Canudo, and Àngel Galobart.
The species name kuehnei honors Walter Georg Kühne, the discoverer of the holotype specimen.
In contrast, Abditosaurus was significantly larger and lacked physiological adaptations to an island environment, suggesting it was a recent immigrant to the ecosystem.
Abditosaurus is associated with the oospecies Fusioolithus baghensis, which closely resembles sauropod eggs found in Gondwana.
Abditosaurus is classified within the family Saltasauridae.
Abditosaurus is classified within the subfamily Saltasaurinae.
The discoverers interpreted Abditosaurus as a member of Saltasaurinae, a clade of titanosaurians found in South America and Africa.
Their phylogenetic analysis determined that the Egyptian sauropod Paralititan is the sister taxon to Abditosaurus, with the Brazilian genus Maxakalisaurus as its next closest relative.

A later study using a revised dataset found that Abditosaurus occupied a different position, not within saltasaurids, but forming a clade with Alamosaurus, Pellegrinisaurus, Baurutitan, and Dreadnoughtus closely related to lognkosaurians.
The parent group of Abditosaurus is Saltasauridae.
Abditosaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
Abditosaurus inhabited the Ibero-Armorican Island, a prehistoric island formed by modern-day Spain, Portugal, and southern France, and was likely the largest titanosaur species in that environment.
Abditosaurus lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Maastrichtian in what is now Europe.
The only known specimen of Abditosaurus was found in the Conques Formation, which dates to the early Maastrichtian of the Cretaceous.
During its time, southern France, Spain, and Portugal formed a single island known as the Iberian-Armoric island.
Abditosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
